topic: converting between exponential and logarithmic forms
subtitle: Rewriting an exponential statement as a logarithm, rewriting a logarithm as an exponential statement, evaluating logarithms by converting, changing base, and solving equations by switching forms

problems.note: Rewrite 5 cubed equals 125 as a logarithm; the exponent is the value of the log.
Rewrite log base 2 of 32 equals 5 as an exponential statement.
Evaluate log base 3 of 81 by asking what power of 3 gives 81.
A negative exponent: 10 to the power minus 2 equals 0.01.
Solve 2 to the x equals 40 by converting to logarithmic form, then estimate.

traps.desc: divided 40 by 2 instead of taking a logarithm

problems.note: A fractional value: 8 to the one third equals 2, so log base 8 of 2 is one third.
Solve log base 4 of x equals three halves by converting to exponential form.
Part (a): change of base written with natural logarithms.
Part (b): use the change-of-base form to approximate log base 3 of 20.

traps.desc: computed the natural log of the quotient instead of the quotient of natural logs

problems.note: Convert log base 5 of (2x minus 3) equals 2 into exponential form, then solve the linear equation.
Doubling time of a 4.5 percent growth model, found by converting to logarithmic form.

traps.desc: divided the doubling factor by the growth factor instead of converting to a logarithm
